profile.title: Deterministic Brownian endpoint comparison for the pulmonary channel case

validity.population: software comparison against the M4.8 pulmonary-bound synthetic tracer case
validity.physiological_state: healthy-adult resting supine capillary context; synthetic local molecular signal
validity.description: Two million independently sampled Brownian endpoints estimate passive-receiver occupancy for the same unbounded free-diffusion case as the analytical channel. The seed and random-stream name make repeated execution reproducible.

limitations: The particle adapter samples exact free-diffusion endpoints and does not retain trajectories or introduce microscopic time steps.
Particles are independent and non-interacting; inertia, collisions, crowding, boundaries, flow, binding, and reactions beyond homogeneous first-order degradation are absent.
The comparison quantifies Monte Carlo agreement with the synthetic analytical case, not agreement with biological or clinical measurements.
The predeclared gate is a software regression criterion; its four-standard-error and 15-percent relative limits are not physiological uncertainty intervals.
N3Sim and AcCoRD motivate and contextualize the independent strategy, but neither external codebase is bundled or executed in M4.9.
